name: Credential Dumping (SafetyKatz / Invoke-Mimikatz)
description: Dump credentials from LSASS using SafetyKatz (minidump-based) or Invoke-Mimikatz. Extracts plaintext passwords, NTLM hashes, and Kerberos tickets.

recommended.note: Use dumped NTLM hash for Kerberos TGT
Create golden ticket with krbtgt hash

notes: SafetyKatz uses minidump approach — less Credential Guard triggering than direct LSASS access. Requires SYSTEM or local admin.

defense.why_it_works: LSASS (Local Security Authority Subsystem Service) caches Kerberos tickets, NTLM hashes, and plaintext credentials (WDigest, if enabled) in memory. SafetyKatz uses a combination of MiniDumpWriteDump API or direct memory reading to extract LSASS memory and parse credentials. Invoke-Mimikatz is the PowerShell wrapper. Both bypass AV by using in-memory execution and indirect syscalls.
defense.prerequisites: Local Administrator or SYSTEM privileges on the target host. An execution channel (PSRemoting, RCE, existing session). LSASS process accessible (not PPL-protected or Credential Guard active).
defense.impact: T1003.001 OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory. Extracts all credentials cached on the host: Kerberos tickets (for Pass-the-Ticket), NTLM hashes (for PtH), cleartext passwords (WDigest), domain account credentials. Directly enables lateral movement to any host where dumped credentials are valid.
defense.detection:
Sysmon Event 10: process access to lsass.exe from non-system processes (common EDR/MDR alert). Sysmon Event 7: Mimikatz DLL loads. Event 4656: handle request on LSASS. EDR: LSASS memory read pattern. Windows Defender: SafetyKatz and Mimikatz signatures. Event 4688: suspicious process creation with lsass in command line.
Processes accessing LSASS memory or SAM registry hives outside of trusted security tools, often followed by file creation or lateral movement (DET0234/AN0648).
Processes opening /proc/*/mem or /proc/*/maps targeting credential-storing services like sshd or login; high privilege escalation and memory inspection tools such as gcore or gdb (AN0649).
Unsigned processes accessing system memory or launching known credential scraping tools (e.g., osascript, dylib injections) to access the Keychain or sensitive memory regions (AN0650).
defense.artifacts: Sysmon Event 10: process accessing lsass.exe from non-SYSTEM source | Event 4656: LSASS handle requested | EDR alert: credential dumping tool signature | Windows Defender alert: Mimikatz | Dump file on disk (*.dmp) if MiniDump used
defense.prevention:
Enable LSA Protection (RunAsPPL): HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RunAsPPL = 1 — makes LSASS a Protected Process Light, blocking all unprotected memory reads. Enable Windows Defender Credential Guard (virtualizes credentials, NTLM/Kerberos material not accessible even with LSASS access). Disable WDigest: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest\UseLogonCredential = 0. Deploy EDR with LSASS access monitoring.
Active Directory Configuration: Manage ACL for 'Replicating Directory Changes All'; add users to Protected Users security group to limit cached plaintext credentials.
Behavior Prevention on Endpoint: Enable Windows 10 ASR rules to secure LSASS and prevent credential stealing.
Credential Access Protection: Enable Credential Guard (Windows 10+) to protect LSA secrets; enable Protected Process Light for LSA on Server 2012 R2.
Encrypt Sensitive Information: Ensure Domain Controller backups are properly secured.
Operating System Configuration: Disable or restrict NTLM; disable WDigest authentication.
Password Policies: Ensure local administrator accounts have complex, unique passwords across all systems.
Privileged Account Management: Do not place domain accounts in local admin groups across systems; limit cross-tier admin use; on Linux restrict root access to prevent memory scraping.
defense.evasion: Use direct syscalls (bypasses API hook-based detectors). Dump LSASS via comsvcs.dll (built-in): rundll32 comsvcs.dll MiniDump. Use a kernel driver to read memory (bypasses PPL). Clone LSASS via Task Manager (if SYSTEM — no MiniDump call).
defense.misconfiguration: RunAsPPL not enabled. Credential Guard not deployed. WDigest enabled (UseLogonCredential = 1) — stores cleartext passwords. No EDR monitoring LSASS access.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# RunAsPPL disabled (default on older Windows):
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa').RunAsPPL
# Returns $null or 0 = PPL NOT enabled = LSASS memory readable

# WDigest enabled (plaintext creds in memory):
(Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest').UseLogonCredential
# Returns 1 = plaintext passwords cached in LSASS
defense.secure_config:
# Enable LSA Protection (PPL):
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name RunAsPPL -Value 1
# Registry entry also requires: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\RunAsPPLBoot = 1 (Secure Boot)

# Disable WDigest:
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest' -Name UseLogonCredential -Value 0
# Via GPO: Computer Config → Admin Templates → MS Security Guide → WDigest: Disabled

# Enable Credential Guard (Windows 10/Server 2016+):
# Computer Config → Admin Templates → System → Device Guard
# → Turn On Virtualization Based Security: Enabled
# → Credential Guard Configuration: Enabled with UEFI lock

# Sysmon Rule — alert on LSASS access:
# <ProcessAccess onmatch='include'><TargetImage condition='is'>C:\Windows\system32\lsass.exe</TargetImage></ProcessAccess>
